name: Cerebral Palsy - Musculoskeletal Complications
definition: Musculoskeletal consequences of cerebral palsy including spasticity, contractures, hip displacement, scoliosis and gait dysfunction.

investigations.principle: Hip surveillance radiographs and condition-specific imaging are used according to age/function.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, tumor or occult-injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific pathway.

amber: Surgery is considered for progressive hip displacement, contractures or deformity affecting function/care.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vata/Bala-related phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Musculoskeletal consequences of cerebral palsy including spasticity, contractures, hip displacement, scoliosis and gait dysfunction.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for rapidly progressive weakness, respiratory/swallowing compromise, major vascular symptoms, suspected malignancy/pathological fracture, severe systemic illness or other listed red flags.
